title: Redwood POC Weekly Sync - Quantaco AI - Cost Econ Review
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on cost/unit economics: token throughput (tokens/sec/$), caching and batching tradeoffs, and next steps to run targeted benchmarks. Redwood reviewed recent benchmark runs showing caching savings and discussed dedicated vs hosted economics for Quantaco's chat workloads.
next_steps: Redwood to share updated cost spreadsheet with tokens/sec/$ breakdown and model variants by 2025-11-21
Quantaco to provide 48-hour full-traffic sample logs for workload mix by 2025-11-24
Schedule deep dive on KV cache tuning (SE-led) for week of 2025-11-24
action_items: Maya Chen: Share cost spreadsheet and benchmark config (due 2025-11-21)
Ravi Patel: Prepare KV cache tuning doc and recommended batch settings (due 2025-11-24)
Omar Saeed: Export 48-hour traffic sample and send to Redwood (due 2025-11-24)
Lena Morales: Confirm P95 latency SLO and top 3 user flows for cost calc (due 2025-11-22)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-19 10:00 PST — Duration 45m — Attendees: Maya Chen, Ravi Patel (Redwood); Lena Morales, Omar Saeed, Priya Nair, Marcus Yu (Quantaco)

00:00 Maya: okay everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep to 45 minutes. today it's the cost econ deep-dive, tokens per second per dollar, caching and batching tradeoffs. quick roll call?
00:07 Lena: hey it's Lena here, hi Omar, Priya, Marcus on.
00:12 Omar: Omar on infra.
00:15 Priya: Priya — CTO.
00:18 Marcus: Marcus here.
00:20 Maya: great. so quick recap from last week, we ran the mixed-workload bench with the 8k context redwood-turbo-1 variant, and we saw about 1.8x savings when prefix caching was enabled for stable user queries. ravi, can you summarize the numbers?
00:36 Ravi: yeah sure, so high level — baseline hosted runs without caching gave us roughly 2,400 tokens/sec on an a100-equivalent instance, cost normalized that is about 0.012 tokens per cent, or put another way ~83 tokens/sec per dollar. with prefix/KV caching on typical dialogs we measured effective token generation up to 190k tokens per minute in aggregate but more usefully that translates to about 1.9x lower token cost for the same traffic mix. transcription note: a100-equivelent was detected as a100e in some logs.
01:15 Lena: okay those raw numbers help. can you break out p95 latency impact when batching is increased? we worry about tail latency for our live chat.
01:23 Ravi: absolutely. when we increased batch window to 50ms to improve throughput, average throughput jumped to ~130 tokens/sec per connection but p95 latency moved from 220ms to about 380ms, so tradeoff there. with smaller batch windows (10-15ms) we keep p95 ~230ms but throughput per GPU drops. also note the batching math depends on request size — our shorter prompt flows don't batch as well.
02:02 Marcus: is that with KV caching enabled?
02:05 Ravi: yes, KV + prefix caching still applied. one subtlety: caching amplifies batching benefits for repeat prefixes because cached kv avoids compute and we just stream tokens back, so the batch can be mostly IO. for unique prefixes the benefit is less.
02:22 Priya: when you say prefix caching, do you mean customer-level session caching? our security team will want clarity on what we store.
02:28 Maya: good callout. for the POC we're using ephemeral KV cache pinned to the model instance and encrypted at rest; cache keys are hashed and no PII is stored. we can provide a writeup for your security team.
02:43 Omar: from infra perspective we want to see the memory footprint — how big are these KV caches per session?
02:48 Ravi: typical conversation history cache for 8k context is ~40-80MB per active session depending on tokenization and whether we store raw vs compressed keys. if you use compression and shard caches you can get that down. note: numbers are approximate, some transcription shows 40 to 80 MG.
03:12 Lena: back to cost econ — can you show the per-model numbers? we've got three model classes in the POC: small fast, baseline, and quality (larger). we want tokens/sec/$ per model.
03:24 Ravi: yes, quick breakdown from latest run (normalized to dollars per hour): small-fast (quantized 4-bit) — ~260 tokens/sec per dollar; baseline 16-bit — ~95 tokens/sec per dollar; quality large — ~32 tokens/sec per dollar. these are aggregate and change with batching and cache hit rate. note the quantized path also reduces memory and increases batch capacity.
04:00 Priya: so quantization looks attractive. what about output quality regressions? have we run regression tests?
04:06 Maya: we've got evals linked in the shared drive — the quality delta for your top flows was within acceptable bounds for small-fast for most queries, a few hallucination cases increased slightly. we flagged those in the eval doc.
04:18 Lena: good. our product metric is task-success rate, if that drops we can't take cost-savings. want to see a side-by-side run.
04:25 Ravi: agreed — recommended approach: run A/B with 10% traffic on quantized small-fast for two weeks and measure success rate + latencies. this will give statistically meaningful numbers.
04:36 Marcus: how does dedicated vs hosted affect these token/$ numbers? we may prefer dedicated if the unit-econ is better.
04:42 Maya: great question. rough rule of thumb: hosted has higher marginal cost but you avoid baseline reserved capacity. for your steady-state chat volume if you commit to dedicated GPUs you can shave ~20-35% off token cost depending on commitment and autoscale patterns. we can model your traffic shape into a dedicated sizing proposal.
04:58 Omar: what's the break-even point for dedicated? monthly tokens or sustained concurrency?
05:03 Maya: typically when you exceed about 3-4M tokens/day with predictable diurnal patterns or sustained concurrency above X vcores/GPUs depending on model. ravi can produce a model-specific break-even using your sample logs.
05:16 Ravi: yeah I'll run the break-even calc. please share 48-hour full traffic sample as discussed.
05:21 Lena: noted. one item — caching gave 1.9x savings in bench, do we have a sensitivity table by cache hit rate? e.g., 30% vs 60% vs 90%?
05:30 Ravi: we do. quick summary: at 30% hit rate savings ~1.2x, 60% ~1.6x, 90% ~2.1x. hit rates depend heavily on user behavior — repeat queries, templated prompts, and session re-use.
05:45 Priya: security/process Q — for private deployment, does caching live in your VPC or on the instance?
05:50 Maya: for Redwood Private we can ensure cache lives in your VPC, controlled by you, with KMS integration and audit logs. for hosted it's in our managed infra but encrypted and customer-segregated. we'll attach a short note clarifying defaults.
06:06 Marcus: any folks mentioned competitors in these tests? sometimes our procurement asks about alternatives.
06:10 Lena: yeah we looked at Replicate and Vertex as comparators.
06:13 Maya: we can provide side-by-side cost numbers for Anthropic and Vertex too but with caveat that direct comparatives are noisy.
06:21 Omar: operational question — when you increase batching window to 50ms we saw improved throughput but p95 increases. is there an adaptive batching policy you recommend?
06:29 Ravi: yes, we recommend workload-aware dynamic batching: short timeout for low latency flows and higher timeout for background/async flows. Redwood runtime supports per-route batching config that you can tune. also warm-starting model instances reduces cold-start latency.
06:44 Lena: do we have an estimate for expected cost savings if we combine quantization + caching + tuned batching? ballpark percent.
06:51 Ravi: ballpark for your mix: quantization (~1.8x), caching (~1.6x at 60% hit), batching tweaks (~1.2x) — combined multiplicative effects aren't purely multiplicative due to overlap but we estimate roughly 3-4x improvement on token cost vs baseline no-caching 16-bit with conservative overlap assumptions. we'll put precise modeled scenarios in the spreadsheet.
07:15 Priya: ok good. next steps for us: security review, send logs, and plan the A/B for quantized variant.
07:22 Maya: recap — Redwood will: 1) share cost spreadsheet with scenario modeling and break-even calc (due 11/21), 2) KV cache tuning doc and batching presets (due 11/24), 3) schedule KV tuning deep dive week of 11/24. Quantaco will share logs and confirm SLOs.
07:40 Lena: sounds good. any blockers on our end?
07:44 Marcus: none currently, just timing on logs export.
07:47 Omar: will try to get logs earlier but 11/24 is realistic.
07:50 Maya: perfect. last thing — we'll also include a short note on audit logs and encryption for security. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep dive.
07:58 Priya: thanks all.
08:00 meeting end.
